goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 uses open(url) on an unauthenticated user-controlled URL without blocking private/reserved IPs or validating redirects, enabling SSRF against internal services

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48, the code uses `open(url).read` where `url` comes from user input (the embed_url parameter). The `open` method from Kernel (or open-uri) will fetch arbitrary URLs including internal/private IP addresses like 127.0.0.1, 169.254.x.x (AWS metadata), 10.x.x.x, etc. This is a classic Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. An attacker could provide URLs like 'http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/' to access cloud metadata services, or 'http://localhost:6379/' to interact with internal Redis, or scan internal network services. The code only validates that the URL starts with 'http://' or 'https://' (line 11) but doesn't block private/reserved IP ranges or validate that redirects don't lead to internal services.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:37 imports feed HTML verbatim, and Post#cook leaves raw_html posts unsanitized, enabling persistent same-origin XSS

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in poll_feed.rb line 37, content is processed with `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed to `TopicEmbed.import()`. In topic_embed.rb, the import method calls `PostCreator.new()` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. In post.rb, the cook method returns `raw` directly when cook_method is raw_html: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. This means RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization. The content from external RSS feeds could contain malicious JavaScript, and since it's rendered as raw_html, it would execute in users' browsers. This is a real XSS vulnerability - external content is trusted and rendered without sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:6 limits embed_url to 255 characters, causing longer valid URLs to fail creation and remain indefinitely on the loading view

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the migration file db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb, the embed_url column is defined as `t.string :embed_url, null: false`. In Rails, a string column without an explicit limit defaults to 255 characters in most databases. However, the finding claims this is at line 6, but the actual definition is at line 5. More importantly, while URLs can theoretically be longer than 255 characters, this is a design decision rather than a clear bug. The code doesn't show any explicit 255 character limit being set - it's using the default string type. Additionally, URLs over 255 characters are relatively rare in practice, and many systems use similar limits. This is more of a potential edge case concern rather than a clear defect that would cause immediate problems. The finding is speculative about what 'longer valid URLs' would fail without demonstrating this is a real issue in the codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve even though the controller now calls Jobs.enqueue, causing the controller test suite to fail

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, in embed_controller.rb line 14, when topic_id is nil, the controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. However, in the test spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb lines 41-46, the test expects `TopicRetriever.new.retrieve` to be called directly. The test mocks TopicRetriever but the controller actually enqueues a job (Jobs::RetrieveTopic) which internally calls TopicRetriever. This is a mismatch - the test is mocking the wrong thing. The test expects TopicRetriever to be instantiated directly in the controller, but the controller delegates to a background job. This would cause the test to fail because TopicRetriever.expects(:new) would never be satisfied since the controller calls Jobs.enqueue instead.
